name: Fire a power shot
summary: On its own key, the unit fires one heavy special shot that hits far harder than its ordinary weapon, then waits out a cooldown. Most versions show a wind-up first, a moment of aiming or charging that the target or the enemy team can see, and some pay with stored energy instead of, or as well as, a cooldown. The shot often adds one twist: it goes through everything in a line, reaches further than the normal gun, ignores armour or stuns. Its job is a burst of damage at a chosen moment: picking off a key target, breaking a defence or catching a row of enemies. Unlike the charge-up weapon trait, it is a separate shot on its own key, not the ordinary gun held to charge; unlike switch-weapon-mode, it is one shot, not a lasting change.
counterplay: Watch for the wind-up and step out of the line or behind cover before it fires.
Hit the shooter during its wind-up: some versions are cancelled by damage, and it cannot fire its normal weapon meanwhile.
Turn untargetable during the wind-up if an ability allows it: one lock-on version keeps its target revealed even through invisibility, but is called off when the target can no longer be targeted.
Push right after it fires: the cooldown or the spent energy leaves a window in which the big threat is gone.
Block or absorb it with a shield where one is available.

other_examples.note: Once a research upgrade unlocks it, the capital ship picks one target, charges for a few seconds and then fires a single huge blast that only the toughest units survive; no splash, long cooldown. Its long reach makes it a siege tool against static defences and anti-air it outranges.

The Ghost spends energy, aims at one biological target for over a second, then fires a sniper round that ignores armour. Taking damage during the aim, or the player's own order, cancels it, and a later patch refunds the energy when it fails; it cannot be lined up on several targets in a queue. It replaced the older Snipe ability in Legacy of the Void.

sources.title: Template:SC2SteadyTargeting, StarCraft Wiki (Fandom)
sources.version: StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void, patch 4.0.2 for the refund

other_examples.note: Every commander can drain a large lump of stored energy to supercharge its main gun for one shot: a big blast with the gun's normal reach, full damage against shields, useless against aircraft and submerged units, with a short lockout between shots. How much energy you store decides how often you can fire; its damage is held low against other commanders and buildings for balance.

The heavy tank's offensive special ability fires one special shell that is strong against light armour but weak against heavy armour, and then recharges; a special-ammunition version where the shot changes what it is good against rather than just hitting harder.

sources.title: M1A1 Abrams, World in Conflict Wiki (Fandom)

shooter_analogues.note: This titan's ordnance is charged before release. In its close-range mode the blast knocks back and damages enemies near it; in its long-range mode it is a projectile that hurts every enemy along its path with a small explosion. Players charge it behind a corner and then step out; some enemy shields can absorb or catch it.

In this top-down action game, Sniper's ultimate locks onto one enemy, aims for a short while and then fires a heavy shot at very long reach that briefly stuns. From the moment aiming starts, the target carries a mark everyone can see and stays revealed to Sniper's team, so turning invisible does not save it; the aim is called off if the target enters a special untargetable state that a few abilities give (the wiki calls it hidden). It refreshes when it kills a hero, and an upgrade makes it faster with a longer stun.

player_translation.summary: Besides its ordinary gun, the unit has one big shot on a key: aim, wind up for a moment that everyone can see, then fire a round that hits many times harder, often through a whole line of enemies. Then it waits out a cooldown.
as_user: Save the shot for the moment that matters: a wounded heavy, an enemy hero, or a squad lined up in a corridor.
Wind up behind cover and step out to fire, so the enemy has less time to react to the warning.
During the wind-up you are a target, and in some versions a hit cancels it, so pick a safe angle.
After the shot your big threat is gone for a while; fall back on your ordinary gun or reposition.
as_target: A visible aim line or charging glow tells you a big shot is coming and from where.
Step off the line, break line of sight or duck behind hard cover before it fires.
Rush or shoot the shooter during the wind-up, or push right after the shot while its cooldown runs.
teammates: Setup and finisher: a teammate who stuns, slows or pins an enemy sets it up for the shot, or the shot softens a heavy for teammates to finish.
Enemies with shields or quick dashes become counter-picks to a power-shot unit.
A teammate's smoke or cover lets the shooter wind up safely.
controls: Q: start the wind-up toward your aim; the shot fires when it completes (or hold Q and release to fire once charged).
Primary fire stays the ordinary weapon; the power shot never replaces it.
Stored-energy variant: the key greys out until enough energy is banked.
feedback: From above, a thin aim line or a growing glow on the barrel shows the wind-up and its direction to both teams.
The target, or everyone near the line, gets a warning marker while the shot charges.
A heavy, distinct report and a bright tracer along the shot's path, with every enemy hit flashing.
The key's cooldown shows on the shooter's HUD; enemies can learn it from the sound.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS originals the shot is clicked onto a unit and never misses; for a player it should be aimed (a line or a projectile) so the target can dodge it.
The wind-up must be visible from a top-down camera and long enough to react to, otherwise it is unanswerable burst damage.
Some RTS versions lock onto a target from far outside its sight (Yamato, Assassinate); in a shooter the target needs a warning and a chance to break line of sight.

Iron Harvest's Change Log #20 made the Piercing Shot fire reliably and take priority over other actions; a player's shot should likewise fire when the wind-up ends, not depend on the AI's next action.

team_play.notes: The power shot is strongest when a teammate holds the target still or lines enemies up, and it softens heavies for others to finish. It is mostly a personal tool, so the enemy answers it with shields, mobility and pressure during the wind-up.

notes: A second fire action with its own cooldown, wind-up state and damage; most of it reuses the ordinary weapon's hit code.
Line-piercing needs a ray or projectile that keeps going after a hit and lists everything on its path, decided on the server.
Wind-up visuals and warnings must be sent to every client in range so targets can react.
Burst damage that kills from full health with too short a warning feels unfair; keep the wind-up readable and the damage below a full kill on most targets.
Several power-shot units firing together erase anything; the cooldown and wind-up keep them from chaining.
A long-reach power shot can let a unit outrange defences it should have to approach (the Yamato's job), so reach must be tuned with the map.
A wind-up glow and a big tracer are easy to read from above.
Players must know which enemies carry a power shot, so the unit's silhouette or barrel should show it.

variants.name: Wind-up shot
variants.summary: The base form: aim for a moment, then fire one heavy round on a cooldown.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Anna Kos Piercing Shot; StarCraft II Battlecruiser Yamato Cannon

variants.name: Piercing line
variants.summary: The round goes through everything in its path, so a row of enemies can all be hit by one shot.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Anna Kos Piercing Shot; Titanfall 2 Legion's long-range Power Shot

variants.name: Stored-energy shot
variants.summary: The shot drains a large lump of a stored energy pool, so how much you bank decides how often you can fire.
variants.seen_in: Supreme Commander commander Overcharge; StarCraft II Ghost Steady Targeting (energy)

variants.name: Interruptible aim
variants.summary: Taking damage during the aim cancels the shot and gives back what it cost, so enemies can stop it by hitting you.

variants.name: Marked lock
variants.summary: Lock onto one enemy at long reach: from the start of the aim the target carries a mark everyone can see and stays revealed to the shooter's team, so ordinary hiding or invisibility does not stop the shot; an untargetable state that a few abilities give (Dota's hidden) calls it off.

variants.name: Special shell
variants.summary: The shot is a different kind of round that trades power against heavy armour for power against light targets, or the other way round.
variants.seen_in: World in Conflict M1A1 Abrams HEAT shell

variants.name: Close blast
variants.summary: In your close-range mode the same key releases a short blast that knocks back and hurts enemies around the muzzle instead of a long shot.

variants.name: Refresh on kill
variants.summary: A kill with the shot resets its cooldown, rewarding a well-chosen finisher.
variants.seen_in: Dota 2 Sniper Assassinate (refreshes on a hero kill)

adds_strengths.why: One heavy hit at a chosen moment, far stronger than the ordinary weapon, to pick off a key target or a row of enemies.

adds_weaknesses.why: The wind-up warns the target and leaves the shooter exposed, and after the shot the cooldown leaves a window to push.

counters.why: Only the toughest units survive a Yamato blast, and the Piercing Shot can hurt mechs from behind, so heavies lose their safety margin.
The Yamato's long reach lets it hit static defences from outside their range.

countered_by.why: Shields absorb or catch the shot: Titanfall 2's sword block and vortex shield both answer Legion's Power Shot.
Reasoned: StarCraft II's Ghost loses the shot when damaged during the aim, so a fast attacker that reaches the shooter mid-wind-up stops it.

open_questions: Should the power shot be aimed and dodgeable (a line or projectile) or lock onto a target as in the RTS originals? (Recommended: aimed, with a visible wind-up.)
Should damage during the wind-up cancel it, as for the StarCraft II Ghost? That rewards pressure but frustrates the shooter.
Should stored energy be its own resource on a card, or should the cooldown carry all power shots?

shooter_fit.reason: A heavy aimed shot on a key is a staple of hero shooters and action games (Titanfall's Legion, Dota's Sniper): easy to build, easy to read from above with a wind-up line, and skill-based on both sides.
